7	marked `[CRITICAL]`.
8	
9	This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
10	boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.
11	
12	## Why a contract is written rather than generated
13	
14	A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
15	— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
16	repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
17	so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
18	the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
19	had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
20	says how the refusal is declared now).
21	
22	So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
23	output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
24	generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.
25	
26	**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**
27	
28	- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
29	  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
30	  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
31	- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
32	  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
33	  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
34	  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
35	- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
36	  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
37	- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
38	  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
39	  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.
40	
41	The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
42	dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
43	the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
44	would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
45	template that is three paths, six operations and eight schemas — and refusals with codes had
46	to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
47	`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.
48	
49	## Compatibility mode
50	
51	A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
52	after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
53	one of three values in its own `README.md`:
54	
55	| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
56	|---|---|
57	| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
58	| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
59	| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |
60	
61	Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
62	code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.
63	
64	## Four boundaries, three directories
65	
66	| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
67	|---|---|
68	| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
69	| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
70	| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
71	| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |
72	
73	**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
74	gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
75	ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
76	the application does not create the schema itself —
77	[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
78	directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
79	first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
80	beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.
81	
82	## What enforces this
83	
84	| Check | What it holds |
85	|---|---|
86	| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
87	| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
88	| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
89	| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |
90

# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts

A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
marked `[CRITICAL]`.

This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.

## Why a contract is written rather than generated

A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
says how the refusal is declared now).

So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.

**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**

- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.

The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
template that is three paths, six operations and eight schemas — and refusals with codes had
to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.

## Compatibility mode

A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
one of three values in its own `README.md`:

| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
|---|---|
| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |

Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.

## Four boundaries, three directories

| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
|---|---|
| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |

**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
the application does not create the schema itself —
[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.

## What enforces this

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |

122

124	
125	- **For the orchestrator — the recorded tier signals are out of date.** Q-8 lights

129	- **For the requirements author — the tie-break.** Newest first (Q-6) needs a rule for two

132	- **For the design stage — the words and the frame.** The user asked for no particular address
133	  for the list, no particular form of navigation and no particular copy (only that it is
134	  English, Q-7). The lockup's product name "Guestbook", the footer about entries and the 404
135	  sentence all describe a one-screen guestbook application
136	  (`frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx:24`, `:72`; `system-states.md`, line 134).
137	  What they say with two screens is the mock-up's decision, for the user to approve there.

    environment starts with).
  - **This reaches `scripts/`.** `impact.md` recorded `tooling_touched` as absent on exactly
    this condition: "reached only if the requirements give the list seed data" (§ What I
    could not determine; § Tier signals). The condition is now met. See § Open.

Round 3, the read-back:

- **Q-9 — Is the summary right, including the assumptions for the smaller details?** →
  **Looks right, go ahead.** The summary was read back in plain words, together with the eight
  assumptions below, and the user confirmed all of them. They are settled, not assumed:
  - **A task is one line of text, up to 200 characters.** An empty task, or one made only of
    spaces, is refused. (The guestbook's trimming and counting rule, `BR-01`, is the nearest
    precedent. How the 200 is counted is the requirements author's to state.)
  - **Deleting asks "are you sure?" first,** as deleting a guestbook entry does, and a deleted
    task is gone for good (no bin, no undo).
  - **Editing changes the text only, never done or not done.** A done task can be edited too.
  - **The same text can be added twice**, and that makes two separate tasks.
  - **All tasks are on one list:** no search, no pages, no filters such as "only open", and no
    "clear all done" button.
  - **No due dates, priorities, assigned people, categories or multiple lists.** It is one
    shared list.
  - **When two people change the same task at the same moment, the later change wins.** A
    task somebody else has already deleted gives a clear message that it no longer exists.
  - **The list does not update live** while somebody looks at it. They see other people's
    changes when the list reloads.

## What the user said and the system does differently

- *Nothing.* Every answer stays inside what the specification allows. Q-1 keeps the guestbook,
  which `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` (lines 17-19) calls the example the first real feature
  replaces. That is a choice the specification leaves open, not a conflict with it.

## Rules no document carried

- **A task's "done" can be undone** (Q-2). Today no stored thing in this system has a state:
  a guestbook entry "either exists or it does not" (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`).
  The to-do list brings in the first stored state, and it is reversible.
- **Ticking done never moves a task** (Q-4, Q-6). The list has one order, newest first, and
  done or not done plays no part in it.
- **Editing a task leaves its done-ness alone** (Q-9). The text and the state are two separate
  things, changed separately.

## Deliberately out of scope

- **Removing or changing the guestbook** — the user chose to keep it (Q-1).
- **A Polish screen** — the screen is English, like the rest (Q-7).
- **Search, paging, filters and "clear all done"** — one list, everything on it (Q-9). The
  guestbook's `BR-05` stays the guestbook's.
- **Due dates, priorities, assigned people, categories and more than one list** — one shared
  list of one-line tasks (Q-9).
- **Live updates** — the list shows other people's changes when it reloads (Q-9).
- **Accounts, logins and "my tasks"** — the standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md`
  § Deliberate non-goals) holds for the to-do list as it does for the guestbook: anybody may
  add, tick, edit and delete any task.

## Open

Nothing here blocks the requirements. Each item has a named owner:

- **For the orchestrator — the recorded tier signals are out of date.** Q-8 lights
  `tooling_touched`, which `impact.md` recorded as absent on the condition Q-8 has now met. The
  tier does not move (`new_context` alone gives p3). The record should say what the change
  reaches before the design stage reads it.
- **For the requirements author — the tie-break.** Newest first (Q-6) needs a rule for two
  tasks added at the same instant, the way `BR-04` gives the guestbook one. It is a detail of
  the order, not a new product choice.
- **For the design stage — the words and the frame.** The user asked for no particular address
  for the list, no particular form of navigation and no particular copy (only that it is
  English, Q-7). The lockup's product name "Guestbook", the footer about entries and the 404
  sentence all describe a one-screen guestbook application
  (`frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx:24`, `:72`; `system-states.md`, line 134).
  What they say with two screens is the mock-up's decision, for the user to approve there.

# How this works today

*Descriptive only. No proposals — this is what the requirements author reads before
anyone decides anything.*

## What the request touches

The request (`request.md`, line 5, Polish, verbatim) asks for a to-do list: anybody can add a
new task, a task can be marked as done, one simple view with a field for adding tasks and a
list of the tasks added, and beside each task a way to mark it done and — "ew." — to delete or
edit it. In the glossary's words the system today has exactly one bounded context,
**Guestbook**, whose one stored thing is an **Entry** (`spec/glossary.md`, lines 14-15).
Neither *task*, *to-do* nor *done* is a domain word anywhere in the specification. The nearest
existing thing is an Entry — free text an unidentified person adds, amends and deletes — and
an Entry has no state beyond existing (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`). The request
therefore reaches: the set of bounded contexts (a concept no context owns), the route register
and the HTTP contracts, the schema (whose one table is declared "the only table"), the page
frame (a second screen where the frame says there is one), and the system-level non-goals that
bind every screen.

## What the specification says

**The system has one context, and the specification says so in three places.**

- "The only bounded context of this system and the only feature it has" —
  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, line 13; "The only bounded context of this system" —
  `spec/glossary.md`, line 14; "One domain context and one supporting technical slice" —
  `spec/design/architecture.md` § Contexts and their boundaries (line 27).
- The guestbook is an example the template expects to be deleted "when your first real feature
  replaces it" — `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, lines 17-19; `spec/design/architecture.md`
  § What this is, and for whom (lines 13-16); `CLAUDE.md` § What is an example.

**The path a new feature takes is written down.**

- Model, schema, service, router plus one line in `app/api.py`, the context's public API, a
  migration, a screen plus a route in `frontend/src/router.tsx`, `spec/contexts/<context>.md`
  plus entries in `api.md` and `data-model.md`, `contracts/openapi/<context>.yaml`, "one line
  in `.github/CODEOWNERS`", and proof in a unit test, an integration test and a `.feature`
  scenario — `spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new feature adds (lines 496-508).
- A second context shares exactly three files with the first: `app/api.py`,
  `app/contexts/__init__.py`, `frontend/src/router.tsx`, one appended line each —
  `spec/design/architecture.md`, lines 510-514.
- A context declares its neighbours as `<context>:<role>:<pattern>`; the guestbook declares
  `neighbours: []` — `spec/design/architecture.md` § Rules between contexts (lines 57-64);
  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, line 5 and § Boundaries.
- One file per layer, named after the concept, under the owning context; never `utils.py` /
  `helpers.py` — `spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend — where a file goes (lines 42-50); the
  frontend is cut the same way, `frontend/src/contexts/<name>/{pages,components,hooks,lib}` —
  § Frontend — where a file goes (lines 143-147).
- The tactical-modelling threshold: the domain "scores one or two", and "four operations on one
  table do not need an aggregate" — `spec/design/architecture.md` § When a context deserves
  tactical modelling (lines 578-584).

**Standing non-goals that bind every change and every screen.**

- Nobody is identified: no accounts, sessions or roles; "anybody may do anything" —
  `spec/design/architecture.md`, lines 18-23. The system-level wording in
  `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals (lines 123-129) is "anybody may add, amend and
  delete any entry" — the guestbook's noun. No route returns `401`/`403` —
  `spec/design/api.md` § Conventions (lines 39-41). Authentication and personal data require a
  human decision — `spec/constitution.md`, Article XI (lines 154-155).
- No moderation (`spec/invariants.md`, line 145); no mobile version (lines 158-161); no data
  retention policy — "an entry lives until somebody deletes it" (lines 162-163); one database
  engine (lines 164-168). Paging and search were lifted for the guestbook alone, as `BR-05`
  (lines 146-150).

**Data.**

- Every primary key is a UUID generated application-side — `spec/design/data-model.md`
  § Identifiers (lines 66-73); `contracts/invariants/guestbook.md` § `D-03`. `D-01`…`D-03` are
  written in the guestbook's invariants file and swept over the whole of `Base.metadata`, not
  over one table — `spec/design/testing.md`, line 217.
- Every schema change is an Alembic revision with a working `downgrade`; `create_all()` is
  forbidden — `spec/design/data-model.md` § Owner of the schema (lines 9-16). Every schema change
  declares a compatibility mode; a new table is `backward compatible` — § Compatibility mode
  (lines 238-247).
- `guestbook_entries` — "The only table. No relations, no foreign keys, no lookup tables." —
  `spec/design/data-model.md`, lines 93-95. § Migrations: "One revision, and it is the head" —
  lines 212-219.
- Every text field is normalized to NFC, trimmed of a written 30-code-point set and measured in
  code points; `app/platform/schemas/text.py` is declared "a fact about EVERY text field this
  API accepts", while each bound lives beside its own model — `spec/design/conventions.md`,
  lines 91-99; `spec/design/api.md`, lines 146-154.

**HTTP.**

- The `/api` prefix is applied in `app/api.py` and nowhere else — `spec/design/api.md`,
  lines 27-30. A path identifier is a UUID and a non-UUID is a `422` — lines 33-35. Moments are
  ISO-8601 with an offset — lines 36-38. An empty collection is a `200` with empty `items`,
  never a `404` — lines 187-191. Every refusal carries a stable code and a finished English
  sentence kept beside the endpoint — § Refusals (lines 193-208).
- The route register names each route's context: `/api/health` (—), `/api/guestbook-entries`,
  `/api/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}` (`guestbook`) — `spec/design/api.md` § Routes and their
  contexts (lines 43-55).
- Every `/api/*` path the application serves falls under a prefix some contract claims, or the
  comparison fails — `contracts/README.md`, lines 41-47; `contracts/openapi/README.md`,
  lines 36-40. Two contracts exist, both Backward: `guestbook.yaml` (version `1.3.0`) and
  `health.yaml` — `contracts/openapi/README.md`, lines 7-8.

**Screens.**

- One document per screen under `spec/design/ui/`, front matter `route`, `info_ref` (`S-xx`),
  `requirements` — `spec/design/ui/README.md` § Naming. A change touching a screen delivers a
  mock-up at `spec/changes/<CR>/design/ui/index.html` — § HTML is the evidence (lines 9-10).
  Every component lists the states that exist — § Why states are enumerated.
- The frame is one centred column with no top bar and no navigation: "a product that adds a
  second screen **must add navigation here**" (`PageFrame`) — `spec/design/ui/system-states.md`
  § One column (lines 17-24) and § Out of scope. Every screen renders its own `PageFrame`; there
  is no layout route — lines 26-28.
- Copy that states a one-screen application: the 404 sentence "There is one screen in this
  application: the guestbook." (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md`, line 134), the footer
  "Entries are public and editable by anyone with this link." (line 132), `/` redirects to
  `/guestbook` (line 153). "The browser stores nothing" — no `localStorage`, no cookie —
  lines 156-157.
- The whole repository, interface copy included, is English — `spec/design/conventions.md`
  § Language (lines 297-304). The request is written in Polish.

**Decisions and history.** `spec/ADR/index.md` records no decision. `spec/changes/INDEX.md`
lists no earlier change touching a to-do list; the one merged feature change is `CR-2609-9b1e`
(the guestbook).

## What the domain document says

Only the guestbook context exists, and none of its rules or flows names a task.

- `P-01` — leaving and maintaining an entry: adding, reading, amending, deleting. "There are no
  intermediate states, no lifecycle, no transitions to police. An entry either exists or it does
  not." — `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`.
- `BR-01` — an entry requires a signature and a message; values are trimmed before they are
  measured; at most 80 / 1000 code points after NFC — `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`.
- `BR-02` — an amendment moves the moment of amendment and never the moment of writing;
  "edited" is derived — § `BR-02`.
- `BR-03` — deletion is permanent; deleting somebody else's entry is possible; a second deletion
  refuses — § `BR-03`.
- `BR-04` — a total order, newest first by default, ties on the identifier, reversible —
  § `BR-04`.
- `BR-05` — narrowing by a phrase, reading a piece at a time, two counts — § `BR-05`.
- `S-01` — the guestbook screen at `/guestbook` — `spec/design/ui/guestbook.md`, front matter.
- There is no `I-xx` defect space in this repository: the identifier spaces are `P`, `BR`, `S`,
  `D`, `ADR`, `CR`, `R` (`spec/glossary.md` § Identifiers and their spaces), and no `I-NN`
  identifier occurs under `spec/` outside `spec/changes/`.

## What the code does

**Backend.**

- One context is registered, `from app.contexts import guestbook` —
  `app/contexts/__init__.py:20`; importing it is what fills `Base.metadata` before Alembic reads
  it — `alembic/env.py:11`, `app/contexts/guestbook/__init__.py:11`.
- The router aggregate includes the health router, then one line per context —
  `app/api.py:39` and `app/api.py:42`; there is no access check on it — `app/api.py:24`.
- The context's public API exports the model and the two length constants, not the routers —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/__init__.py:21`.
- `GuestbookEntry`, table `guestbook_entries`: `id` (`Uuid`, `default=uuid.uuid4`), `author`
  `String(80)`, `message` `Text`, `created_at` / `updated_at` `DateTime(timezone=True)`; the
  ordering index is declared in the model as well — `app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py:36`.
  No column in the schema stores a state, a flag or a boolean —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py:45`.
- Schemas: separate `Create` / `Update` / `Read` / `Page` classes; `Author` and `Message` are
  `NormalizedText` with `min_length=1` and the model's bound —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/schemas/guestbook_entries.py:50`; `PAGE_SIZE_MAX = 100`,
  `PAGE_SIZE_DEFAULT = 20`, `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH = 200` —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/schemas/guestbook_entries.py:28`; the sort is a closed `StrEnum` —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/schemas/guestbook_entries.py:54`.
- The service opens a `SessionLocal` per call, raises `GuestbookEntryNotFoundError` and names no
  status code — `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:42`; one clock, `_now()` —
  `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:46`; `create_entry` stamps both moments
  with one instant — `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:190`; `update_entry`
  applies the fields given and stamps `updated_at`, with no version check, so the last write
  wins — `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`; `delete_entry` refuses a
  missing id — `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:229`.
- Five operations on `/guestbook-entries` and `/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}`; refusal codes
  `guestbook_entry_not_found` (`404`) and `guestbook_entry_empty_patch` (`422`), sentences as
  constants beside the endpoints — `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py:99`,
  `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py:115`. Domain exceptions are translated
  with `try` / `except` — `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py:157`,
  `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py:189`,
  `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py:203`.
- One revision, `a1b2c3d4e5f6`, with no parent: it creates the table and the ordering index;
  `downgrade` drops the index, then the table —
  `alembic/versions/a1b2c3d4e5f6_create_guestbook_entries_table.py:24`.

**Frontend.**

- Three routes: `/` redirects to `/guestbook`, `/guestbook` renders `GuestbookPage`, `*` renders
  `NotFoundPage` — `frontend/src/router.tsx:28`. The only route constant is `GUESTBOOK_ROUTE` —
  `frontend/src/routes.ts:18`.
- `PageFrame`: the lockup links to `GUESTBOOK_ROUTE`, `PRODUCT_NAME = 'Guestbook'`, a fixed footer
  about entries, no navigation — `frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx:24`,
  `frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx:44`,
  `frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx:72`.
- `NotFoundPage` says "There is one screen in this application: the guestbook." —
  `frontend/src/pages/StatusPages.tsx:14`.
- The guestbook screen: a composer card on top — `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:156`;
  a list of cards with in-place editing, at most one open (`editingId`) —
  `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:59`,
  `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:190`; deletion behind a confirmation
  dialog — `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:228`; a toast after each
  write — `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:109`; the empty state is drawn
  by the page itself — `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx:208`.
- One TanStack Query hook per resource with a keys object; every mutation invalidates the
  resource's keys — `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/hooks/useGuestbookEntries.ts:63`,
  `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/hooks/useGuestbookEntries.ts:193`. Mutations never retry —
  `frontend/src/main.tsx:37`.
- Browser copies of the bounds, held equal to the Python literals by a fitness test —
  `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/guestbookEntry.ts:22` (`spec/design/data-model.md`,
  lines 155-160).
- Shared primitives any screen can use: `Button` / `LinkButton`, `Skeleton`, `ErrorState`,

1	# Requirements — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done
2	
3	**Change:** CR-2609-823a
4	**Source:** request.md, impact.md, brainstorm.md (answers `Q-1`…`Q-9`)
5	
6	## Goal
7	
8	Anybody who opens the application can reach a second screen, a shared to-do list, add a task
9	of one line, tick it done and back, correct it and delete it, while the guestbook stays where
10	it is and keeps working as it does today.
11	
12	Words used below, none of which is in `spec/glossary.md` yet (giving them a home is the design
13	stage's job): a **task** is one line of text somebody put on the list; **the to-do list** is the
14	one list of tasks every visitor shares; **done** and **not done** are the one state a task has,
15	switched both ways; **the moment of adding** is when the system stored a task. It orders the
16	list and never changes.
17	
18	## Success criteria
19	
20	| Id | Criterion | Baseline | How measured after delivery |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **SC-1** | A person who has never seen the to-do list reaches it from the guestbook, adds a task and finds it at the top of the list, with no instruction. | None. Nobody can add a task today: no to-do concept exists in the specification or in the code (`impact.md` § What is missing). | The requester follows the `uat.md` script on the delivered branch before merging and records pass or fail per step. That is the one look after delivery this template schedules. |
23	| **SC-2** | Two people looking at the list after a reload see the same tasks, in the same order, with the same done marks. | None. The guestbook is the only thing people share today, and it has no state anybody marks. | The requester checks it at UAT with two browser windows (`uat.md`). The scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-3` and `CR-2609-823a/R-9` re-check it on every CI run of the branch. |
24	| **SC-3** | A task ticked done by mistake goes back to not done in one action, and neither action moves it in the list. | None. Nothing the application stores has a state that can be switched (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`: "An entry either exists or it does not"). | A `uat.md` step at UAT, plus the scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-4` on every CI run. |
25	| **SC-4** | A reviewer who opens a freshly created environment sees example tasks on the list without typing any. | A freshly created environment opens today with the guestbook's welcome entries (`golden-set/seed/entries-welcome.json`) and nothing else. | The reviewer opens the first preview of this branch (Actions → Preview), or runs `./scripts/start.sh` on a fresh clone, and counts the example tasks. This is manual because the black box starts with `--no-seed` (`R-11`). |
26	| **SC-5** | A guest who knows the guestbook finds it where it was: the main address still opens it and everything it did before still works. | The main address redirects to the guestbook (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Interactions). The 22 scenarios in `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` pass. | The existing guestbook suites run unchanged on every CI run of this branch (the same 22 scenarios plus the UI smoke), and the requester checks at UAT. |
27	
28	## Requirements
29	
30	### R-1: Adding a task — **P1**
31	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want to add a task by typing one line, so
32	that it joins the shared list of things to do.
33	**Why this priority:** Without it there is no list. Every other requirement acts on a task this
34	one creates.
35	**Independent test:** Add one task to an empty list and read the list back.
36	
37	1. The system SHALL present one screen holding one field for a new task's text, with the list of
38	   tasks below that field (`request.md`: "a simple view with a field for adding tasks and a list";
39	   `Q-6`: "right under the field").
40	2. The system SHALL let anybody who opens the to-do list add a task, with no account and no
41	   sign-in.
42	3. WHEN a person submits a text for a new task, the system SHALL store one task holding that
43	   text as `R-2` shapes it, record it as not done, and record its moment of adding.
44	4. WHEN a task has been added, the system SHALL show it first in the list without the person
45	   reloading the screen.
46	5. WHEN a person submits a text identical to the text of a task already on the list, the system
47	   SHALL store a second, separate task (`Q-9`).
48	
49	**Acceptance**
50	- **R-1.1** GIVEN an empty to-do list, WHEN a person adds the task "Water the plants", THEN the
51	  list holds exactly one task, its text is "Water the plants", and it is shown as not done.
52	- **R-1.2** GIVEN a list holding the task "Buy bread", WHEN a person adds "Buy bread" again,
53	  THEN the list holds two tasks with that text, and marking one of them done leaves the other
54	  not done.
55	- **R-1.3** GIVEN a list of two tasks, WHEN a person adds a third, THEN the third is shown first
56	  without the page being reloaded.
57	- **R-1.4** GIVEN a request to add a task that arrives already claiming to be done, WHEN it is
58	  stored, THEN the new task is not done.
59	
60	### R-2: What is not a task is refused — **P1**
61	**Objective:** As a reader of the list, I want empty and over-long texts kept out, so that the
62	list never shows a row with nothing in it.
63	**Why this priority:** It is the other half of `R-1`. Shipping `R-1` without it stores empty
64	rows on the first day.
65	**Independent test:** Submit a text of three spaces and confirm the list is unchanged.
66	
67	1. The system SHALL normalize a task's text to Unicode NFC and trim both of its ends of the
68	   written 30-code-point whitespace set, before it measures the text. This is the rule the
69	   system already applies to every text field it accepts (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend,
70	   on `app/platform/schemas/text.py`; the set is defined in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`).
71	2. IF a task's text is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and
72	   tell the person that a task needs text.
73	3. IF a task's text is longer than 200 code points after normalizing and trimming, THEN the
74	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person that the text is too long.
75	4. WHERE a text carries whitespace other than a line break between its first and last visible
76	   character, the system SHALL keep that whitespace unchanged. (A line break inside the text is
77	   an open question, `D2` in § Open questions.)
78	5. The system SHALL accept on the screen exactly the texts the service accepts. The field
79	   SHALL NOT block, cut short or silently stop taking a text the service would store, and the
80	   screen SHALL NOT let through a text the service would refuse.
81	
82	**Acceptance**
83	- **R-2.1** GIVEN the text "   " (three spaces), WHEN it is submitted as a new task, THEN it is
84	  refused, the person is told why, and the list is unchanged. The same holds for the empty text.
85	- **R-2.2** GIVEN a text of exactly 200 code points, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted
86	  and stored whole. GIVEN one of 201 code points, THEN it is refused and the list is unchanged.
87	- **R-2.3** GIVEN a text of 200 × U+1F600 (200 code points, 400 UTF-16 code units), WHEN it is
88	  typed or pasted into the field and submitted, THEN the screen takes every character and the
89	  service stores the task. GIVEN 201 of them, THEN the screen and the service both refuse it,
90	  for the same reason.
91	- **R-2.4** GIVEN a text of 200 letters, each written as U+0065 followed by U+0301 (400 code
92	  points before normalizing, 200 after), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as
93	  200 code points.
94	- **R-2.5** GIVEN a text of 200 code points with two spaces before it and two after (204 as
95	  typed), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as the 200 code points without
96	  the spaces. GIVEN a text of 205 spaces, THEN it is refused as empty, not as too long.
97	- **R-2.6** GIVEN the text "Buy  two   lamps", WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is stored with its
98	  inner spaces exactly as typed.
99	
100	### R-3: One shared list, in one order — **P1**
101	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want every task on one list in the order
102	the tasks were added, newest first, so that everybody reads the same list the same way.
103	**Why this priority:** The list is what a person looks at. Without a settled order two people
104	see two different lists, and a task just added gets lost among the others.
105	**Independent test:** Add three tasks, then read the list from a second browser.
106	
107	1. WHEN the to-do list is opened, the system SHALL show every stored task, done and not done
108	   alike, on one list, with no division into pages and no filter (`Q-9`).
109	2. The system SHALL order the list by moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`).
110	3. WHERE two tasks share a moment of adding, the system SHALL show them in the same relative
111	   order every time the list is read, so that the order is total.
112	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, or its text is edited, the system SHALL keep it in
113	   the same position in the list (`Q-4`, `Q-6`).
114	5. WHEN the list is opened or reloaded, the system SHALL show the tasks exactly as they are
115	   stored at that moment, including tasks other people have added, marked, edited or deleted.
116	6. WHEN the list holds no task, the system SHALL say that it is empty, with a sentence about what
117	   to do, and SHALL NOT present it as an error (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Components and their states:
118	   "Emptiness always carries a sentence about what to do").
119	
120	**Acceptance**
121	- **R-3.1** GIVEN the tasks "First", "Second" and "Third", added in that order, WHEN the list is
122	  opened, THEN it shows "Third", "Second", "First".
123	- **R-3.2** GIVEN two tasks with the same moment of adding, WHEN the list is read twice, THEN both
124	  reads show them in the same relative order.
125	- **R-3.3** GIVEN 101 stored tasks, WHEN the list is opened, THEN all 101 are shown on one list,
126	  with nothing to press to see more. (101 is one more than the largest piece the guestbook's read
127	  hands out, and more than its default piece of 20.)
128	- **R-3.4** GIVEN the list "Third", "Second", "First" with "Second" not done, WHEN "Second" is
129	  marked done, THEN the list still reads "Third", "Second", "First". The order is also unchanged
130	  after the text of "Second" is edited.
131	- **R-3.5** GIVEN person A has the list open, WHEN person B adds a task and A reloads the list,
132	  THEN A sees B's task first.

440	### Races
441	- **W-1: an edit against a mark on one task.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the stored
442	  task (text and state), replaces the text and writes the whole task back. Between that read and
443	  that write the mark has stored "done". What the database holds at that moment is "done", and
444	  the edit's write-back replaces it with the "not done" it read. `R-9` clause 2 and `R-6`
445	  clause 2 forbid that outcome. The only update path in the codebase today overwrites with no
446	  version check (`impact.md`, `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`), so
447	  nothing in the store holds this rule yet (constitution, article VI). Only a concurrent test can
448	  tell the two apart (`spec/design/testing.md` § Choosing what proves what).
449	- **W-2: two marks from screens that are out of date.** The read-then-write happens if a mark is
450	  built as "read the state, store its opposite". A reads not done and stores done. B, who saw not
451	  done on the screen, reads done and stores not done. The database ends "not done", although both
452	  people chose done. `R-4` clause 3 (record the chosen state) removes the read.
453	- **W-3: an edit or a mark against a delete.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the task (it
454	  exists), the delete removes it, then the edit writes. What the database holds at that moment is
455	  no task. A write that creates on absence brings the task back. `R-8` clause 1 ("create no task")
456	  forbids it.
457	- **W-4: two adds in the same instant.** There is no read. Both tasks are stored with the same
458	  moment of adding, and only a tie-break makes the order total (`R-3` clause 3).
459	- **W-5: filling a new environment against a person adding.** The read-then-write: filling reads
460	  "the to-do list is empty", a person adds a task, then filling posts the example tasks. The
461	  database ends with the person's task plus the examples. No constraint stands behind the check.
462	  The guestbook's filling has the same exposure today, and it is rare, because it only happens in
463	  the seconds after a new environment comes up.
464	- **W-6: two fillings of one environment.** Deploy and preview both run on one environment.
465	  Both read "empty" and both post, so the examples appear twice. This is rare, and the guestbook
466	  has the same exposure today.
467	
468	### With no defined behaviour
469	- **`D1`:** When the to-do list is empty but the guestbook already holds entries, is the to-do
470	  list filled with example tasks? This covers an environment that existed before this change
471	  (stage, an open preview) and one where somebody deleted every task.
472	- **`D2`:** What happens to a text with a line break inside it? It can be sent only through the
473	  API: is it refused, stored as given, or stored with the break replaced?
474	- **`D3`:** Is one of the example tasks done, so that a new environment shows both states?
475	- When a person presses "add" a second time before the first add is answered, does the second
476	  press add a second task, or is it held off until the first is answered?
477	- After an add fails, does the field keep what was typed? After an add succeeds, is the field
478	  emptied?
479	- What does the screen show while a write waits 30 s for its answer, and can the person act on
480	  other tasks meanwhile?
481	- Is there a largest number of tasks the list holds or shows? With no pages (`Q-9`), every task
482	  is read at once, and nothing bounds how many there are.
483	- After "the task no longer exists" (`R-8`), does the list drop that task at once or on the next
484	  reload?
485	
486	## Impact analysis
487	
488	- **Collisions with invariants:** none requires anything to bend. Each source was checked:
489	  - `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals. Authentication: consistent, since anybody adds,
490	    marks, edits and deletes any task (`R-1` clause 2). CSRF: consistent, since there are no
491	    sessions. Moderation: consistent. A mobile version: consistent, since the new screen is not
492	    designed for a phone. A data retention policy: consistent, since a task lives until somebody
493	    deletes it (`R-7`). A second database engine: consistent. Paging and search, lifted for the
494	    guestbook alone as `BR-05`: consistent, since the to-do list has neither (`Q-9`).
495	    **Finding, not a collision:** the authentication and retention items are worded for entries
496	    ("anybody may add, amend and delete any entry"; "An entry lives until somebody deletes it"),
497	    so their wording no longer covers everything the system stores. Only the convergence round
498	    edits this file (its own § Deliberate non-goals), so this is reported and not fixed.
499	  - `contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`. `D-01`: consistent. A done task stays one record in
500	    its place (`Q-4`, `R-3.4`). A design that moved done tasks into a second store would breach
501	    it, and `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py::test_no_table_is_shaped_like_an_archive`
502	    sweeps every table. `D-02`: consistent, since a task points at nothing and copies nothing.
503	    `D-03`: consistent, since nothing here asks for an identifier a person reads. `D-04`:
504	    consistent, since `R-2` holds a task's text to the same normalization, trim set and unit. As
505	    written, `D-04` names the guestbook's two text fields, so it does not by itself cover a task.
506	    Whether an invariant of the task's own domain carries it is the design stage's call.
507	  - Constitution. Article VI: no uniqueness rule exists here (duplicates are allowed, `R-1`
508	    clause 5), so no index is asked for. What has to hold under concurrency is `R-9` clause 2
509	    (race `W-1`). Article XI: no new personal-data field. The example tasks follow the corpus rule
510	    "unambiguously artificial" (`golden-set/README.md`). Article XIII: nothing outside the
511	    allowed stack.
512	- **Decisions that already settle this:** `spec/ADR/index.md`, read whole, records no ADR, and
513	  its `Supersedes` and `Aliases` columns are empty. The rulings that settle parts of this change
514	  live in normative documents, per `spec/design/conventions.md` § When a decision is an ADR:
515	  - `spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend makes `app/platform/schemas/text.py` "a fact about
516	    EVERY text field this API accepts". That settles how the 200 is counted (`R-2`). Consistent.
517	  - `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters, decision of 2026-09-17: "Every bound in
518	    this document is in CODE POINTS". Consistent.
519	  - `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column: a second screen "must add navigation here".
520	    Consistent: `R-5` is that navigation. § Out of scope ("Navigation. One screen, so there is
521	    nothing to switch between") stops being true, which is a design edit.
522	  - `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Interactions: the main address redirects to the
523	    guestbook, and "The browser stores nothing". Both consistent (`R-5` clause 3; `R-3` clause 5).
524	  - `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens, decision of 2026-09-16: the 4.5:1 floor.
525	    Consistent (`R-4` clause 6).
526	  - `spec/design/ui/guestbook.md`, decision of 2026-09-17: no field stops at its bound. This is
527	    the guestbook screen's decision. `R-2` clause 5 asks the same observable of the new field.
528	    Consistent.
529	  - `spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new environment starts with, decision of 2026-09-05:
530	    filling goes through the application, never into production, never into a guest book that
531	    already has entries, and it treats "an environment nobody has written in yet" as one
532	    condition. `R-11` clauses 1–4 are consistent with it. `D1` is exactly where the "one
533	    condition" wording and the per-guestbook refusal stop giving the same answer.
534	  - `spec/design/conventions.md` § Language: English. Consistent (`Q-7`).
535	  - `spec/design/data-model.md` § Identifiers, decision of 2026-08-30. Consistent.
536	- **Dependencies:**
537	  - Exist: the page frame, the shared text rule (`app/platform/schemas/text.py`), the
538	    environment filler, and the toast and error primitives (`impact.md` § What the code does).
539	  - Do not exist, and none blocks: navigation between screens, which `R-5` asks for. A
540	    checkbox or toggle primitive (`impact.md` § What is missing): conventions add a primitive
541	    with its first caller. A browser-side text rule outside the guestbook's own folder:
542	    `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.ts` sits inside the guestbook context, and
543	    `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py::test_no_screen_reaches_into_another_contexts_folder`
544	    refuses a second context that reaches it. Where the rule goes depends on which context owns
545	    a task.
546	  - `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § Deliberate non-goals (authentication, moderation, search
547	    relevance, CSRF): nothing here depends on any of them being built.
548	  - Inherited disagreements (`impact.md` § Where these disagree), none of which blocks the
549	    requirements. First, `spec/design/conventions.md` § Layers says a router translates in a
550	    `match` block and names the guestbook router as the worked example, while that router uses
551	    `try`/`except`, and it is the file a new resource is told to copy. Second,
552	    `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` lists an empty-state primitive that the code removed, and
553	    `R-3.6` needs an empty-list sentence.
554	  - `R-11` reaches `scripts/seed_golden_set.py` and the seed half of the corpus. `impact.md`
555	    recorded `tooling_touched` as absent, on the condition that `Q-8` has since met
556	    (`brainstorm.md` § Open).
557	- **Frozen rules** (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md`):
558	  - `BR-01`: consistent. `R-2` borrows its trim set, NFC and unit and departs from none of them.
559	    The 200 is a new bound, not an edit of 80 or 1000.
560	  - `BR-02`: written about an entry's two moments, so it does not apply as written. `R-6`
561	    clause 2 keeps the moment of adding fixed in the same spirit.
562	  - `BR-03`: consistent. `R-7` clause 2 and `R-8` clause 2 mirror it for tasks.
563	  - `BR-04`: consistent. `R-3` clause 3 asks for the same totality. The to-do list is read in
564	    one direction only.
565	  - `BR-05`: does not apply, since the to-do list has no search and no pieces.
566	  - `P-01`: "There are no intermediate states, no lifecycle" describes entries. If the design
567	    places tasks inside the guestbook context, that sentence stops describing the whole context.
568	  - No departure from any of them, so no ADR with `supersedes` is needed.
569	- **Tests that would fail:**
570	  - `tests/unit/test_guestbook_entry_model.py::test_this_schema_holds_exactly_one_table` asserts
571	    `set(Base.metadata.tables) == {"guestbook_entries"}`. It goes red on any stored task.
572	  - `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_every_corpus_file_is_named_by_the_locator` goes red
573	    until a task seed file is registered in `tests/_golden_set.py`. Once the file is registered
574	    in `SEED_FILES`, these go red:
575	    - `::test_every_entry_carries_the_keys_an_entry_has`, which demands the two guestbook keys;
576	    - `::test_every_entry_meant_to_pass_really_passes` and
577	      `::test_no_seed_entry_stands_near_a_published_limit`, which index `author` and `message`;
578	    - `::test_the_corpus_exercises_a_message_with_line_breaks`, which demands a line break in
579	      every sequence file. This runs straight into `D2`.
580	
581	    `::test_the_corpus_exercises_characters_outside_ascii` stays green only if an example task
582	    carries a character above U+007F.
583	  - `tests/tooling/test_seed_golden_set.py::test_an_empty_environment_gets_the_whole_seed_corpus`
584	    derives its expectation from `SEED_FILES` and reads `author` from every item.
585	    `::test_a_guest_book_with_entries_is_left_alone` expects nothing posted to an environment
586	    whose guestbook holds entries, and **goes red under `D1` option A**.
587	  - `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py::test_the_built_spa_boots_and_a_deep_link_resolves` and
588	    `::test_an_unknown_address_says_so` look up the link named exactly "Guestbook" and call it
589	    "the only navigation this application has". A navigation link with that same name would make
590	    the lookup ambiguous. Whether that happens depends on the name the design chooses.
591	    `::test_the_root_redirects_to_the_one_screen` stays green (`Q-5`), though its name stops
592	    being true.
593	  - `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_frontend_reads_no_corpus_file` names one
594	    frontend module as the only reader of `golden-set/fixtures/text-measurement.json`. It goes
595	    red if the to-do screen's own text-rule test reads that file from somewhere else.
596	  - `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py::test_no_screen_reaches_into_another_contexts_folder`
597	    goes red if a to-do screen in its own context imports the guestbook's browser text rule.
598	  - `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` does not go red. It holds three bounds and their
599	    one browser copy, so a fourth bound and its copy would stand unheld unless the test is
600	    extended.
601	  - `tests/integration/test_migrations.py::test_the_models_and_the_migrations_describe_the_same_schema`
602	    stays green only if the new model and the new revision agree. The guestbook-specific tests
603	    in that file are unaffected.
604	  - `tests/fitness/test_context_declarations.py` and `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py`
605	    stop being vacuously true once there is a second context or table, and go red on an
606	    incomplete declaration.
607	  - `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` (22 scenarios, `CR-2609-9b1e/R-1`…`R-7`) is
608	    unaffected, because nothing here changes the guestbook.
609	- **Other changes in flight:**
610	  - `CR-2609-8ef9` (draft, chore). Its request names `spec/design/testing.md` § What only CI can
611	    answer and `scripts/test.sh`. This change's design stage will edit `spec/design/testing.md`
612	    too (other sections) and reaches `scripts/seed_golden_set.py` through `R-11`. That is the
613	    same document but a different section, and different scripts.
614	  - `CR-2609-9b1e` is merged. Its requirements are cited by `guestbook.feature`, and nothing here
615	    renumbers or edits them.
616	
617	## Non-Goals
618	- **Removing or changing the guestbook.** The user chose to keep it beside the list (`Q-1`), and
619	  every guestbook behaviour and suite stays as it is (`SC-5`).
620	- **A Polish screen or any translation.** The screen is English, like the rest (`Q-7`,
621	  `spec/design/conventions.md` § Language).
622	- **Search, pages, filters (for example "only open tasks") and a "clear all done" action.**
623	  Everything is on one list (`Q-9`). `BR-05` stays the guestbook's.
624	- **Due dates, priorities, assigned people, categories and more than one list.** It is one shared
625	  list of one-line tasks (`Q-9`).
626	- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is reloaded (`Q-9`, `R-3`
627	  clause 5). Nothing pushes them to an open screen.
628	- **Accounts, sign-in, "my tasks", and recording who added or ticked a task.** This is the
629	  standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals): anybody adds, marks, edits and
630	  deletes any task.
631	- **Moderation.** The same standing non-goal: no reports, no hiding.
632	- **Warning a person that somebody else's change overwrote theirs.** "The later change wins"
633	  (`Q-9`), and nobody is told their change was replaced (`R-9`).
634	- **A bin, undo, or restoring a deleted task.** "Gone for good" (`Q-9`, `R-7` clause 2).
635	- **Moving done tasks to the bottom or into a separate section.** Ticking never moves a task
636	  (`Q-4`, `R-3` clause 4).
637	- **Reordering tasks by hand.** The order is the moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`), and
638	  nothing else sets it.
639	- **A mobile design of the new screen.** This is the standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md`
640	  § Deliberate non-goals, "A mobile version").
641	- **A retention policy for tasks.** This is the standing non-goal: a task lives until somebody
642	  deletes it.
643	- **Detecting a duplicate caused by a retried add.** The same text twice is two tasks by
644	  decision (`Q-9`, `R-1` clause 5), so `E-20` leaves a duplicate for a person to delete.
645	
646	## Bounds
647	
648	| Quantity | Value | Where it comes from |
649	|---|---|---|
650	| Task text, maximum | 200 code points, after NFC normalization and trimming | `Q-9` ("up to 200 characters"). The unit is the one every text field is measured in (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend on `text.py`; `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters) |
651	| Task text, minimum | 1 code point after trimming | `Q-9` ("An empty task, or one made only of spaces, is refused") |
652	| Trim set | the written 30-code-point set | `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`, `app/platform/schemas/text.py` |
653	| Emoji boundary value | 200 × U+1F600 = 200 code points = 400 UTF-16 code units; 201 refused | `R-2.3`, from the `D-04` incident |
654	| Decomposed boundary value | 200 × (U+0065 U+0301) = 400 code points before NFC, 200 after | `R-2.4`, from `BR-01`'s normalization |
655	| Padding boundary value | 2 + 200 + 2 = 204 as typed, accepted; 205 spaces, refused as empty | `R-2.5`, from the `api.md` trim-order incident |
656	| Tasks shown per read | all of them, with no pages | `Q-9` |
657	| List size that proves "no pages" | 101 tasks | one more than 100, the guestbook's largest piece (`spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters), and more than its default of 20 |
658	| Example tasks, minimum | 3 | `Q-8` ("a few"), with the seed-half rule that a list is at least three items (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_seed_half_shows_a_list_rather_than_an_entry`) |
659	| Example task, maximum length | under 150 code points (0.75 × 200) | the seed-half margin in `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_no_seed_entry_stands_near_a_published_limit` |
660	| Contrast of a done task's text | at least 4.5:1 against the surface behind it | `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens (WCAG 2.1, 1.4.3) |
661	| "At the same moment" | both changes sent before either is answered | `R-9` |
662	
663	The search phrase's bound is also 200 code points (`QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`). That is two rules
664	sharing a number, and a test that reads the phrase's constant to prove the task's bound proves
665	the wrong rule.
666	
667	## Open questions
668	- **`D1`: example tasks when the to-do list is empty and the guestbook is not.** This blocks
669	  the design of `R-11` and the change to `scripts/seed_golden_set.py`. It also decides whether
670	  `tests/tooling/test_seed_golden_set.py::test_a_guest_book_with_entries_is_left_alone` changes.
671	  It is for the user.
672	- **`D2`: a line break inside a task's text.** This blocks the contract's refusal set (design
673	  stage, API) and the corpus rule on line breaks
674	  (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_corpus_exercises_a_message_with_line_breaks`).
675	  It is for the user.
676	- **`D3`: whether one example task is done.** This blocks the shape of the seed corpus and
677	  whether filling has to mark a task after adding it. It is for the user.
678	- **Double add while the first is in flight, what the field holds after an add, the screen while
679	  a write waits, the list after "no longer exists", and a largest number of tasks.** None of
680	  these blocks the requirements. They are for the design stage: the screen specification and the
681	  mock-up the user approves. A product rule the design needs from them goes back to the user,
682	  not into a design document.
683	- **The frame's words with two screens: the lockup name, the footer about "entries", the header
684	  fact, and where the not-found page leads.** These block nothing here. `brainstorm.md` § Open
685	  gives them to the mock-up, for the user to approve there. `R-5` clause 4 is the only
686	  constraint on them in this document.
687	
688	## Self-check
689	
690	1. [Completeness] [§ R-1] Does the moment of adding need to be visible to anybody, or does it
691	   serve only the order? If a person has to see it, the screen needs a requirement and the
692	   mock-up a place for it. As written, it serves `R-3` alone.
693	2. [Coherence] [§ R-1] Is "a new task is recorded not done, whatever the request claims" a rule
694	   the user stated, or one inferred from "a to-do list"? If a reviewer calls it invented, it goes
695	   to the user. The rejected reading is that a client can add a task already done.
696	3. [Clarity] [§ R-2] Can a second implementer find "the written 30-code-point set" without
697	   reading guestbook code? It points at `BR-01` and `text.py`. If tasks land in another context,
698	   the set has to be shared rather than copied, or two copies drift.
699	4. [Completeness] [§ R-2] What happens to a line break inside a text? It is open (`D2`). Until it
700	   is answered, clause 4 says nothing about line breaks, and `R-2.6` uses spaces only.
701	5. [Measurability] [§ R-2] Can "the screen takes every character" in `R-2.3` be observed in a
702	   suite that owns citations? It can over the rule the screen applies, in vitest. The typing and
703	   pasting half only the UI smoke sees, and the smoke owns no citation. If design finds no vitest
704	   seam, that half loses its automated proof.
705	6. [Compliance] [§ R-2] Does `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` hold the new 200 and its
706	   browser copy? No, it names three bounds. Unless it is extended, the new copy stands unheld, as
707	   the signature's unit did before `D-04`.
708	7. [Clarity] [§ R-3] Does "newest first" still mean "by moment of adding" after an edit? Yes, by
709	   clause 4. A reader who takes "newest" as "most recently changed" makes edited tasks jump, and
710	   `R-3.4` pins the intended reading.
711	8. [Completeness] [§ R-3] Is there a number of tasks beyond which "every task on one list" stops
712	   being acceptable? None is stated. If the design needs a ceiling, that is a product question for
713	   the user, not a design choice.
714	9. [Measurability] [§ R-3] Can `R-3.2` be observed without control of the clock? Only if a test
715	   can store two tasks with an equal moment of adding. Otherwise the tie-break passes by luck.
716	10. [Clarity] [§ R-4] Is "mark done" setting a chosen state, or flipping the stored one? It is
717	    written as setting (clause 3). A flip built by the design fails `R-4.3` and `R-9.3` under
718	    screens that are out of date.
719	11. [Coherence] [§ R-4] Does clause 6 restate a rule that already has a home
720	    (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens)? Yes, on purpose, as the observable form of the
721	    defect this screen invites. If the frame's floor moves, this clause follows it rather than
722	    competing with it.
723	12. [Measurability] [§ R-4] Can "shown differently" be judged without a person? Only through what
724	    a test can read, such as the done state as the page exposes it. The visual form belongs to the
725	    mock-up.
726	13. [Completeness] [§ R-5] Where does the not-found page lead when there are two screens? That is
727	    not stated. If it leads only to the guestbook, a visitor who wanted the to-do list is one step
728	    further away, which `R-5` does not forbid.
729	14. [Compliance] [§ R-5] Would a navigation link named exactly "Guestbook" break the exact lookups
730	    in `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`? Yes: two links with one name. The design either names the link
731	    differently, or the smoke's locator changes in the same change.
732	15. [Coherence] [§ R-6] Does "leave the task's state as it is stored at that moment" contradict
733	    "the later change wins"? Only if "later wins" is read as applying to the whole task. It is
734	    read per aspect (text, state). If the user meant the whole task, `R-9` clause 2 is the
735	    sentence to take back to them.
736	16. [Completeness] [§ R-7] Does the confirmation have to name the task? That is not stated. The
737	    guestbook's dialog does name the entry (`spec/design/ui/guestbook.md` § The delete dialog), so
738	    the mock-up will likely copy it. It is not a requirement here.
739	17. [Clarity] [§ R-8] Does "tell the person the task no longer exists" require the list to drop
740	    that task at once? No, and it is open. If the design leaves it on screen, a second attempt
741	    meets the same message.
742	18. [Clarity] [§ R-9] Is "the change applied later" well defined when two requests overlap? It
743	    means the one whose write the store applied last. If a reviewer needs arrival order instead, a
744	    mechanism beyond the store's own ordering is needed.
745	19. [Measurability] [§ R-9] Can `R-9.1` be proved by a sequential test? No. An edit followed by a
746	    mark passes over a whole-task write-back too. Only concurrent requests tell the two apart
747	    (constitution, article VI).
748	20. [Completeness] [§ R-10] Is the typed text still in the field after a failed add? That is open.
749	    If it is not, the person retypes it, and nothing here says whether that is acceptable.
750	21. [Completeness] [§ R-11] What happens in an environment that existed before this change and
751	    whose to-do list is empty? That is `D1`. Option A turns
752	    `tests/tooling/test_seed_golden_set.py::test_a_guest_book_with_entries_is_left_alone` red.
753	22. [Compliance] [§ R-11] Is `**Verified-by:** manual` honest here, or does a citation-owning
754	    suite exist that proves it? `tests/tooling/` and `tests/fitness/` own no citation, and the black box runs
755	    with `--no-seed`. If design-testing finds a surface, the marker has to be removed, not left
756	    standing beside a test.
757	23. [Coherence] [Gap] Do the non-goals in `spec/invariants.md`, worded for entries, bind the to-do
758	    list? By intent yes, by wording no. Only the convergence round edits that file, so the finding
759	    goes there.
760	24. [Compliance] [Gap] Which bounded context owns a task? That is not a requirement: it is
761	    design-domain's call. If tasks live inside the guestbook context, the closing sentence of
762	    `P-01` ("An entry either exists or it does not") stops describing that context.
